title: HB 933 (2019 Regular Session): Voter Identification; revise time to provide after casting an affidavit ballot.
operative_text:
(a_in_person_id)
(section) Sec. 1 (23-15-563(1))
(quote) Each person who appears to vote in person at a polling place or the registrar's office shall be required to identify himself or herself to a poll manager or the registrar by presenting current and valid photo identification before such person shall be allowed to vote.
(section) Sec. 1 (23-15-563(2))
(quote) (a) A current and valid Mississippi driver's license; (b) A current and valid identification card issued by a branch, department, agency or entity of the State of Mississippi; (c) A current and valid United States passport;
(b_no_id_remedy)
(section) Sec. 1 (23-15-563(3)(a))
(quote) A person who appears to vote in person at a polling place and does not have identification as required by this section may vote by affidavit ballot. The affidavit ballot shall then be counted if the person shall present acceptable photo identification to the registrar * * * by 5:00 p.m. on the second day after the election day
(section) Sec. 1 (23-15-563(3)(b))
(quote) An elector who has a religious objection to being photographed may vote by affidavit ballot, and the elector, * * * by 5:00 p.m. on the second day after the election day, shall execute an affidavit in the registrar's office affirming that the exemption applies.
(section) Sec. 2 (23-15-573(1))
(quote) or that he or she is unable to present an acceptable form of photo identification: (a) A poll manager shall notify the person that he or she may cast an affidavit ballot at the election.
(section) Sec. 2 (23-15-573(2)(b))
(quote) then the poll manager shall write "NO ID" across from the voter's name and in the appropriate column in the pollbook.
(c_mail_ballot_id) not stated.
(d_proof_of_citizenship) not stated.
(e_other_rule)
(section) Sec. 1 (23-15-563(4))
(quote) The intentional failure of an election official to require a voter to present identification as required by this section shall be considered corrupt conduct under Section 97-13-19 and shall be reported to the Secretary of State and the Attorney General.
(other) Sec. 2 (23-15-573): affidavit ballot procedure reprinted; ID-less voters get written notice of how to learn if the ballot counted; Secretary of State uniform affidavit envelope; statewide tracking by reason
(other) Time to present ID shortened (from five days) to 5:00 p.m. on the second day after the election; same deadline for the religious-objection affidavit and for obtaining a Mississippi Voter Identification Card
